title: 1.1: Identifies that DocumentClassifier uses SHA1 hash comparison (self.data_hash vs new_data_hash) in the train() method as the retraining decision mechanism
1.2: Reports that predict_correspondent() returns the highest probability class without any minimum confidence threshold as the prediction acceptance behavior
1.3: Identifies that RasterisedDocumentParser invokes OCR via ocrmypdf.ocr() Python API as the OCR invocation method
1.4: Identifies that DirectoriesMixin setUp() calls setup_directories() to create isolated temporary directories for test isolation

1.5: Reports that training occurs after the training-document inserts in the test setup, through an explicit train_classifier() or DocumentClassifier.train() call (e.g., test_one_correspondent_predict_manydocs creates its documents with Document.objects.create() and only then calls self.classifier.train())
1.6: Lists OCR parameters passed to ocrmypdf: language, output_type, use_threads, jobs, progress_bar, and skip_text/force_ocr based on OCR_MODE for the OCR configuration
1.7: Reports that mime type is detected via magic.from_file(path, mime=True) before parsing as the mime type detection method
1.8: Identifies that pytest.mark.skip decorator is ignored by Django's unittest test runner, causing test_load_classifier_cached to execute unexpectedly as a source of non-deterministic test behavior

1.9: Reports that 2 documents are created from a PDF with one separator barcode (patch-code-t-middle.pdf) and 3 documents from a PDF with two separator barcodes (several-patcht-codes.pdf) for barcode splitting behavior
1.10: Identifies 'PATCHT' as the default barcode string value from CONSUMER_BARCODE_STRING setting that triggers document splitting

1.11: Explains that barcode splitting changes the classifier's training data because one input file becomes several Document records, each consumed separately with its own OCR-extracted content (e.g., a PDF with two separator barcodes yields 3 training documents instead of 1, which changes the training data hash)
2.1: Claims that async_task() executes tasks synchronously in production for background task behavior
